key_insight: AA-ViT uses anatomy-, structure-, and frequency-guided vision transformers to synthesize contrast-enhanced brain MRI from pre-contrast scans while better preserving tumour and tissue boundaries.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this approach could reduce reliance on gadolinium contrast, lower scan burden, and improve access to brain tumour imaging when contrast agents are unsuitable.
method: Inputs T1, T2, and FLAIR pre-contrast MRI
Uses an anatomically aware vision transformer with structural and frequency guidance
Aims to preserve fine lesion detail and anatomical boundaries in synthetic CEMRI
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2021, the method reportedly outperformed state-of-the-art baselines on PSNR and SSIM, and received a mean clinical rating of 3.94/5 from three neuroradiologists and one neurosurgeon across 19 cases.
watch_item: The clinical evaluation is small and preliminary, so real-world robustness, generalizability, and impact on diagnostic decisions still need larger prospective validation.
paper_title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis
